units: Ex. R. s. 42, end מיד ליד from hand to hand, directly, opp. ע״י שלוחו through his messenger.—י׳ רחבה a wide hand, liberality.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 1:5:2">Y. Ḥag. I, 76ᶜ</cite> top <he>עני ויָדוֹ ר׳</he> a poor man who is liberal, opp. <he>י׳ מעוטה</he> stingy.—
<cite ref="Chullin 58b">Ḥull. 58ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>בְּיָד</he> on the forefoot (of a quadruped).—
<cite ref="Mishnah Oktzin 1:1">Ukts. I, 1</cite> <he>כל שהוא יד ולא שזמר</he> whatever part of a fruit serves as a handle (as the stem) and not as a protector (as the shell of a nut &c.).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 29:4">Kel. XXIX, 4</cite> <he>יַד הקורדום</he> the handle of an ax; a. v. fr.—
Cant. R. to I, 4 לא חלתה יד ליד hand does not fit hand, i.e. the two cases are incongruous.—Trnsf. an intimation, an incomplete statement intelligible from context, surroundings &c.
Y. Ned. I, 36ᵈ top תופסין אותו משם יד לקרבן we make him responsible because what he said is suggestive of the word korban (as a vow); a. fr.—Du. יָדַיִם; pl. יָדוֹת.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yadayim 1:1">Yad. I, 1</cite> <he>נותנין לי׳</he> is required for pouring on the hands.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yadayim 2:3">Ib. II, 3</cite> <he>הי׳ מטמאות וכ׳</he> hands (when being washed) become unclean or clean up to the wrist; a. v. fr.—<he>י׳ יפות</he>, v. <cite ref="J00500"><he>יָפֶה</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Nedarim 2b:5">Ned. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>ידות נדרים</he> (or <he>ידות</he>) suggestions of vows, contrad. to <he>כינויים</he>, v. <cite ref="K00566"><he>כִּינּוּי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Nedarim 5b">Ib. 5ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>י׳ שאין מוכיחות לא הויין י׳</he> suggestions which are not beyond doubt, are no (binding) suggestions; a. fr.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 70b:8">B. Mets. 70ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="A02056"><he>אֶמְצַע</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 3b:7">Kidd. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>קטנה דלית לה יד וכ׳</he> a minor who cannot accept a betrothal for herself.
<cite ref="Nedarim 88b:4">Ned. 88ᵇ</cite> <he>יד אשה כיד בעלה</he> the wife’s possession is her husband’s possession.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 23a:6">Kidd. 23ᵃ</cite> <he>גיטו ויָדוֹ באים כאחד</he> his letter of manumission and his right of self-disposal come simultaneously.

<cite ref="Yevamot 39a:1">Yeb. 39ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Ketubot 83a:9">Keth. 83ᵃ</cite> <he>ידו כיָדָהּ</he> the husband’s right of disposal is as great as the wife’s (concerning what belongs to her); <he>ידו עדיפא מידה</he> his rights are stronger than hers.

B. Mets. VI, 2 יָדָן על התחתונה their rights are the lowest, i.e. they are responsible for losses but can derive no benefits from favorable chances; ib. כל המשנה ידו על התחתונה וכ׳ whichever side changes the agreement is at a disadvantage, and whichever side breaks the agreement &c.; a. v. fr.—Du. יָדַיִם, constr. יְדֵי.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 41b:12">Ab. Zar. 41ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>מִירֵי ודאי</he>, v. <cite ref="F00014"><he>וַדַּאי</he></cite>.—<he>יְדֵי חובתו</he>, v. <cite ref="J00515"><he>יָצָא</he></cite>.
Tosef. Men. IX, 10 שתי י׳ two thirds; a. fr.—מִיַּד (= מיד ליד) at once, directly, immediately.
Tosef. Dem. VIII, 7, v. חָלַל Hif.—
Y. Pes. VI, 33ᵃ מיד כל מי וכ׳ presently, every one whose Passover offering was a lamb &c.; a. v. fr.— עַל יַד, על יְדֵי (abbr. ע״י) through, by means of.
<cite ref="Gittin 40b:5">Gitt. 40ᵇ</cite> <he>שמא זיכה לו ע״י אחר</he> he may have benefitted him (given him his liberty) through the agency of another person (without the slave’s knowledge).

Nidd. I, 1 מעת לעת ממעטת ע״ו וכ׳ the period of twenty four hours is modified by the interval between one examination and the other (if that interval is less than twenty four hours); a. v. fr.—על ידי ש־ because.
Lev. R. s. 32 ע״י שגדרו וכ׳ because the Israelites guarded themselves against unchastity, they were redeemed; a. v. fr.—עַל יָד עַל יָד gradually, little by little.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 80a:8">B. Kam. 80ᵃ</cite> (opp. <he>מיד</he>); <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 8:15">Tosef. ib. VIII, 15</cite>.

Par. VIII, 7 Hai G. (ed. only once ע״י).—כלאחר יד, v. אַחַי.—יָדַיִם Yadayim, name of a treatise of the Mishnah and Tosefta, of the Order of Tohăroth, containing the laws of levitical cleanness or uncleanness of the hands.
